name: isMFALoggingEnabled
definition: CONTESTED -- four integrations answer 'any audit record came back' with no MFA filter at all (a quiet tenant reads false), while JumpCloud answers 'at least one MFA-marked event came back' (an empty read is not measured). Nothing reads an MFA logging setting. See conflict.positions.
population: unknown -- every audit record in the vendor's default read window at Okta and Azure AD; MFA-marked Directory Insights events at JumpCloud
evidenceRequiredForTrue: unknown until ruled: either at least one audit record of any kind (Okta, Azure AD) or at least one event marked as MFA (JumpCloud: mfa true, mfa_meta, auth_mfa_context, or an event_type containing mfa)

conflict.summary: Five wired integrations, four wired files. The type agrees (boolean); the population does not. At Okta and Azure AD the key name says MFA but the code applies no MFA filter: it is the same affirmative_signal as isAuditLoggingEnabled, and the Okta file emits isIAMLoggingEnabled with the same value from the same read, although the Okta and Azure AD RTA descriptions say 'MFA-related records'. Only JumpCloud filters for MFA events. Both sides are activity proxies; no file reads an MFA logging setting.

positions.meaning: At least one audit record of any kind is returned, or the body carries an explicit on flag. No MFA filter, no recency. An empty read is a measured false.
positions.population: all audit records in the vendor's default read window

integrations.name: Okta
integrations.note: the same file also emits isIAMLoggingEnabled with the same value

positions.meaning: At least one Directory Insights event is marked as MFA (mfa true, mfa_meta, auth_mfa_context, or an event_type containing mfa). No MFA event in a read below the 10000-row cap is a measured false; an empty read, or none at the cap, is not measured.
positions.population: MFA-marked JumpCloud Directory Insights events returned by searchDirectoryAuditEvents
positions.source: File read for this entry; test_jumpcloud_logs_fail_closed.py:101

proposedResolution.summary: Rule this key with isIAMLoggingEnabled, whose open decision already asks whether isMFALoggingEnabled is a separate control or an alias. If separate, the Okta and Azure AD files must filter for MFA events (as JumpCloud does) or leave this key; if an alias, the JumpCloud filter is a stricter meaning that needs its own name.

decision.question: Is isMFALoggingEnabled a distinct control (MFA events are recorded) or an alias of isIAMLoggingEnabled / isAuditLoggingEnabled, given that Okta and Azure AD answer it from every audit record and only JumpCloud filters for MFA events? And what does an empty read mean?
